findings.description: The moved binding code still emits an unsafe runnable order for PARTIAL mappings. A dependency on an unbound unit is discarded by ($u2t[.] // empty), so the dependent is treated as ready; an unbound child implementing the prerequisite can sort after the dependent, and a bound dependent whose prerequisite has no implementing task is emitted as runnable at all.
findings.evidence: Orchestrator-reproduced: jq -nc with U-dependent bound and U-prereq unbound yields [{"task":"T-A-DEPENDENT","dep_tasks":[]}] - the known design edge vanishes. Existing 9j/9n fixtures bind BOTH ends of the real edge and leave only an unrelated third child unbound, so they never exercise this case.
findings.suggested_fix: Refuse the degraded schedule with batches=[] when any dependency of a bound unit lacks a bound implementing task; add a fixture binding the dependent and leaving the PREREQUISITE unbound.

findings.disposition: DEFERRED to claude-workflow-plugin-uopo by operator decision - the prescribed fix IS the json_read primitive
findings.description: All three design record selectors retain the successful-but-empty class: latest_design_artifact_designer accepts rc-0/no-output as legitimate absence; latest_design_review and latest_design_unit_binding accept rc-0 {} as legitimate absence. A call-site malfunction becomes no_design_attempted, design_verdict_missing, or 'no existing binding', permitting duplicate/non-advancing review or binding writes.
findings.evidence: Read :7219-7231, :7264-7295, :8365-8379. Only nonzero rc, nonempty output, and (for reviews) a union containing valid {} are checked. Tests inject nonzero failure or malformed nonempty output, never rc-0 absence sentinels.
findings.suggested_fix: Each selector should emit a required structured envelope such as {retrieved:true,found:boolean,record:...} with exact key/type validation, so computed absence and a successful wrong result are not the same bytes.

findings.disposition: PARTIAL MUST-FIX: the three probed cases in scope; the general 'guarded envelopes everywhere' form deferred to uopo
findings.description: Several safety computations accept a successful empty/container result on outer type alone: ctrl_json/canon_json/caseco_json/dup_json accept []; unit_task_map accepts {}; batching_inputs accepts mutually inconsistent empty sets; batch_result/batches_json accept ok:true with batches:[]. These can hide control/canonical/case collisions or multiply-bound units while reaching parallel_safe:true.
findings.evidence: Read :1553-1664 and :1870-2043. Literal probes: {ok:true,batches:[]} passes the :2025 predicate; {r:[],unresolved:[],blocked:[],ud_r:{}} passes :1935; a forged dup_json=[] passes its array gate while from_entries silently reduces two U1 bindings to {U1:T2}.
findings.suggested_fix: In scope: make dup detection account for every pair, make r+unresolved partition unit_ids exactly, and reject ok:true with batches:[] when children exist.

findings.disposition: MUST-FIX in scope - three sites, one pattern
findings.description: Three authoritative validate-design consumers erase the validator exit status with `|| true` and accept .ok textually. A shape-valid ok:true body exiting nonzero, or ok:"true", is trusted by design-record, design-unit-bind and design-conform - even though epic-gate.sh now correctly refuses those exact cases.
findings.evidence: Orchestrator-verified byte-identical patterns at :6945-6947, :8047-8049 and :8573-8575: `vout=$(... ) || true` then `vok=$(... jq -r '.ok // false' ...)` then `[ "$vok" != "true" ]`. jq -r renders the JSON string "true" as shell text true. epic-gate.sh:1373-1395 demonstrates the required discipline.
findings.suggested_fix: Capture validator rc separately at all three sites, require rc 0, and validate exact envelope types before reading any field.

findings.disposition: MUST-FIX in scope - new round-6 code
findings.description: The new emitter guards validate parseability, not the complete envelope. Any parseable wrong result from the guarded construction ([], null, {}, or an object with missing/wrong fields) prints directly and returns 0. qa-gate.sh print_envelope_checked at :8806 has the same parse-only weakness.
findings.evidence: jq -n -e '[]' returns rc 0, satisfying review-check.sh:662-663 and qa-gate.sh:8806-8807. Round-6 tests sabotage these builds only with exit 5, so the literal fallback is never exercised for rc-0 parseable-wrong output.
findings.suggested_fix: Validate exact subcommand, booleans, required strings, numeric units, array unit_ids and object maps before printing; add legs injecting rc-0 parseable-wrong output.

findings.description: A failure to acquire the flock does not stop the critical section. Because the entire subshell is the left side of `|| rebind_rc=$?`, bash disables errexit inside it, so `flock -x 9` can fail and execution continues through the read and add_comment WITHOUT a lock.
findings.evidence: Static read of :8183-8215 plus probe `set -e; ( false; echo continued ) || rc=$?` which printed continued and ended rc 0, matching the compound-command structure.
findings.suggested_fix: Test `flock -x 9` explicitly and emit an infrastructure refusal before reading or writing when it fails.

findings.disposition: MUST-FIX in scope - the repo's own pairing requirement, already fixed once in the other half this slice
findings.description: The accessor and artifact mutation suites never execute the shipped qa-gate.sh/review-check.sh. They copy all scripts into a fixture and set QG/RC to those copies; no behaviour leg runs the repository artifact. Static SHIPPED_QG greps do not satisfy 'a leg must observe the shipped artifact RUNNING'.
findings.evidence: design-accessors.test.sh:127-131 and :190 assign QG to the fixture copy; design-artifact.test.sh:101-105 and :139-140 do the same for QG/RC. plan-batches.test.sh:297-309 explicitly records why a copied artifact does not satisfy this, after the identical defect (R4-F6) was fixed there.
findings.suggested_fix: Run at least one positive/restore-control behaviour leg per affected script via its canonical repository path with CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR pointed at the fixture; reserve fixture copies for mutants and support scripts.

findings.disposition: MUST-FIX in scope - the claim moved because of round-6's own fixes
findings.description: Docs still say every guard-list degradation collapses to one task per batch. Early degradations that cannot enumerate children, jq-unavailable/envelope-construction failures, pair-encoding failure and topological refusal all emit batches:[] instead. The epic-gate usage/header repeats the broader claim.
findings.evidence: Compared docs/HOOKS.md:2582 and epic-gate.sh:86,467-472 against calls at :1255-1258 and literals at :952/:1202, none of which produce a singleton schedule.
findings.suggested_fix: State that singleton serial batches are emitted only when child ids AND a safe order are available; otherwise batches is explicitly empty.

non_discriminating.why: All behaviour invocations use the fixture copy assigned to QG; no leg runs the repository qa-gate.sh, violating the shipped-artifact pairing requirement.
QG and RC are fixture copies; static reads of SHIPPED_QG do not constitute executing the shipped artifact.
Both inject only a nonzero build failure; they stay green if the non-empty/parseability portion of print_envelope_checked is deleted, and do not discriminate rc-0 parseable-wrong output.
The shim exits 5, so the rc arm alone triggers the fallback; the legs stay green if parseability validation is deleted.

confirmed_discriminating: plan-batches.test.sh 9f.9, 9h and 9n re-targeting now genuinely discriminates their named guards, and their markers are source-unique as asserted.
